translations.title: The tomb of Akr Caar
translations.text:
“I am your soul, Nikoptis. I have velado

These cinco milenios and your eyes muertos

No itself movieron ni never have respondido to my desire,

And your miembros ligeros, that atravesé in llamas,

No have ardido conmigo ni with azafranada cosa some.


Look, the hierba leve itself levantó for make your almohada

And you besó with a miríada of lenguas vegetales;

Mas you no me besaste.

Of so much leerlo gasté the oro of the wall

And fatigué my pensamiento in the signos.

And no there is nothing new in this sitio.


I have sido amable. Look, I have left the cántaros sellados

For if despertabas and murmurabas for your vino.

And I have mantenido suaves the túnicas over your body.


¡Oh despreocupado! ¡How could olvidar!

-Until the river makes so much time,

¿The river? Eras less that young

And three souls vinieron over Ti

And I vine.

And volé over ti, the hice huir;

I have sido íntima contigo, you I have known.

¿Acaso no I have tocado your palms and the puntas of your fingers?

¿Acaso no me I have deslizado to través tuyo until the talones?

¿How entré? ¿Acaso no am I you and You?


And ningún sun comes to socorrerme in this lugar

And estoy torn against the oscuridad tenebrosa;

And ninguna light me golpea and no you say

Word, day tras day.

¡Oh! could salir, to pesar of the marcas

And all your hábil labor over the puerta,

Salir to través of the campos of green cristal…


Mas there is quietud here.

No me voy.”

translations.title: Letanía nocturna
translations.text:
¡Oh Dios, purifica our hearts!

¡Purifica our hearts!

Sí, the líneas that has depositado in mí

in sitios of beauty

and the beauty of this your Venecia

that me has mostrado

provocan my tears.


Oh Dios, ¿what gran bondad

tuvimos in tiempos pasados

and hemos olvidado today,

that us has dado this wonder,

oh Dios of the aguas?


Oh Dios of the night,

¿what gran pain

us acometerá

that us has recompensado

antes of the time of your llegada?


Oh Dios of the silence,

purifica our hearts,

purifica our hearts,

because hemos visto

the glory of the shadow

semejante to your doncella.


Sí, the glory of the shadow

of your beauty has caminado

over the shadow of the aguas

in this your Venecia.

And ante the holiness

of the shadow of your doncella

I have gathered the gaze,

oh Dios of the aguas.


Oh Dios of the silence,

purifica our hearts,

purifica our hearts,

oh Dios of the aguas,

limpia our hearts,

because I have visto

the shadow of this your Venecia

flotando over the aguas,

and your stars


have visto this prodigio, from your remotos cursos

have visto ellas this prodigio,

oh Dios of the aguas,

apacibles as are your stars

mudas for nosotros in your remotos cursos,

serene is also my heart

and itself vuelve silencioso inside of mí.


Purifica our hearts

oh Dios of the silence,

purifica our hearts

oh Dios of the aguas.

translations.title: Commission
translations.text:
Id, songs mías, to the solitario and to the insatisfecho,

id also to the desquiciado, to the slave of the convenciones,

llevadles my desprecio toward your opresores.

Id as a ola gigante of water cold,

llevad my desprecio for the opresores.


Hablad against the oppression inconsciente,

hablad against the tyranny of the that no have imaginación,

hablad against the ataduras,

id to the burguesa that itself is dying of tedio,

id to the women of the barrios residenciales,

id to the repugnantemente casadas,

id to aquellas cuyo fracaso is hidden,

id to the emparejadas without fortuna,

id to the esposa comprada,

id to the woman comprometida.


Id to the that have a lujuria exquisita,

id to aquellos cuyos deseos exquisitos are frustrados,

id as a plaga against the aburrimiento of the world;

id with your filo against esto,

reforzad the sutiles cordones,

traed confianza to the algas and tentáculos of the soul.


Id of manera amistosa,

id with words sinceras.

Ansiad the hallazgo of males new and of a new bien,

oponeos to all the formas of oppression.

Id to quienes the mediana edad has engordado,

to the that have lost the interés.


Id to the adolescentes to quienes les asfixia the familia…

¡Oh, what asqueroso resulta

ver three generaciones reunidas bajo a mismo ceiling!

Is as a tree old with retoños

and with algunas branches podridas and cayéndose.


Salid and desafiad the opinión,

Id against this cautiverio vegetal of the blood.

Id against all the clases of hands muertas.

translations.title: Portrait d'une femme
translations.text:
Vuestra mind and Usted are our sea of the Sargasso,

Londres has soplado over Usted this veintena of años

And barcos brillantes le have left esto or aquello in pago:

Ideas, old habladurías, sobrantes of all layas,

Extraños mástiles of the conocimiento and grises mercancías of valor.


Grandes hombres the have buscado -extrañando to another.

Usted siempre has sido segundona.  ¿Trágico?

No. Usted lo prefirió to the cosa usual:

A man apagado, aburrido and galante,

A mind normal -with a pensamiento less, each año.

Oh, Usted has sido paciente, the I have visto sentada

For horas, in where algo debería haber flotado.

And now Usted paga. Sí, ricamente paga.

Usted is a persona of some interés, uno itself acerca

And itself carries extrañas semillas:

Trofeos rescatados, some curiosa sugerencia;

Hechos that no carry to ninguna parte; a cuento or two,

Preñadas of mandrágoras, or with some another cosa

That could be útil and without embargo never lo is,

That jamás encaja in a rincón or shows utilidad,

Or itself encuentra your hora over the tejar of the días:

The work deslustrado, cursi, maravilloso, old;

ídolos and ámbar gris and the raros embutidos,

Éstas are your riches, your gran depósito; and without embargo,

For all this treasure hundido in cosas momentáneas,

Excéntricas maderas casi empapadas and material new and bright:

In the lento flotador of light diferente and deep:

¡No! ¡No there is nothing! To the fin and to the cabo,

Nothing is suficientemente your.

And without embargo is Usted.

translations.title: Portrait of a woman
translations.text:
Your mind and you are our Sea of the Sargazos,

Londres has flotado in torno to ti durante these últimos años

and brillantes naves you have left esto or aquello as tributo:

ideas, old chismes, pedazos of thousand cosas,

extraños jirones of conocimiento and costosas prendas

desteñidas.

Grandes inteligencias you have buscado −to falta of another

persona.

Has sido siempre postergada. ¿Trágico?

No. Has preferido esto to lo acostumbrado:

a man torpe, aburrido and hogareño,

a mind mediocre −with a pensamiento less each año.


Oh, are paciente. You I have visto sentada

for horas, ahí where algo pudo haber surgido to flote.

And now pagas to uno. Sí, generosamente pagas.

Are a persona of cierto interés, uno comes to ti

and itself carries consigo a strange ganancia:

trofeos pescados, some curiosa sugestión;


datos that no conducen to ninguna parte: a or two historias

preñadas of mandrágoras, or algo that could be of

utilidad and that without embargo never utilizamos,

that no full ningún hueco ni demuestra your uso,

ni encuentra your hora in the woven of the días:

between the deslustradas, llamativas, maravillosas cosas old;

ídolos and ámbar and preciosas incrustaciones,

éstas are your riches, your gran almacén; and without embargo

for all this sea acumulado of objetos inútiles,

extrañas maderas semihumedecidas, and cosas nuevas

and brillantes:

in the lento flotar of diferentes luces and profundidades,

¡no!, ¡no there is nothing! In the suma of all these cosas,

no there is nothing that sea enteramente tuyo.

And without embargo, esto are you.

translations.title: Famam librosque cano
translations.text:
¿Your songs?


¡Oh! The pequeñas madres

the cantarán in the crepúsculo,


and when the night

itself desvanezca to the beso of the dawn

that ama and mata,

the hora that the golondrinas llenan

with your notas, the conejitos of the field

that some llaman children,

tal as are, altos and gordos,

comentarán your besos between risas,

poniéndose the zapatos, listos for the day of negocios,

serios negocios infantiles of the that the world

laughs, and crecen viciados

tal is the relato

−parte of él− of your song-to-the-life.


¿The mío?


A libro is known for aquellos  that leen

the mismo. Your público is presente

in mí arenga. ¡We go! From makes años

the considero my audiencia

tal as antes lo was tuya.


Flaco, with anteojos, without tacones,

tal as uno that feels to the world

as a suerte of maldición against your borrachera

revolcándose in your últimos años for a roja codicia

and without embargo; to all velocidad

aún when debería correr for your propia satisfacción,

itself will return for mofarse

because no tuvo

a centavo, ninguna voluntad for asumir the desastrosas

consecuencias of the Demonio of the Wealth.


Tal as aquel of who itself apartan the women

for the cenizas of tabaco esparcidas over your saco

and cuyo neck

shows poca familiaridad with the navaja of afeitar

and a barba of three días;

tal as aquel that gathers a andrajosa

copia without reverso of the establo,

demasiado barata for be catalogada,

discurso,


“¡Ah-eh! The strange and raro nombre…

¡Ah-eh Debe be if aún I no I have…”

Tal edad

while perdona your hábitos

analiza the forma and piensa in ver

how escapé to the inmortalidad.

translations.title: Only I want be in your bosom
translations.text:
Only I want morir in my land,

that me entierren in ella,

fundirme and desvanecerme in your fertilidad

for resucitar siendo hierba in my land,

resucitar siendo flower

that deshoje a niño crecido

in my country.


Only I want be in the bosom of my homeland

siendo land

hierba

or flower.

translations.title: Cogemos the songs...
translations.text:
Cogemos the songs

of your cansado and derretido heart,

and bajo the denso sea of the tinieblas,

with loving light,

holocaustos e inciensos, the amasamos.

Insuflamos in ellas the strength of the pedernal and of the roca,

and luego the tornamos to your límpido and puro heart,

¡oh, people combatiente and paciente!

translations.title: Dolores of parto
translations.text:
The wind sopla the polen in the night

to través of the ruinas of hogares and campos.

The land itself estremece of love,

with the pain of dar to light,

but the conquistador us quiere make creer

historias of sumisión and rendición.


¡Oh, Dawn Arab!

Dile to the usurpador of our land

that the parto is a strength desconocida for él,

the pain of the body of the mother,

that the land cargada of scars

inaugura life

in the momento of the dawn

when the rose bleeding

florece in the wound.

translations.title: My dear homeland...
translations.text:
My dear homeland

No importa cuánto time you agite the stone

Of the molino of the pain and the agonía

In the páramo of the tyranny,

Ellos never serán capaces

Of arrancarte the eyes

Or kill your esperanzas and dreams

Or crucify your voluntad of levantarte

Or of darle valor to the smile of our children

Or destroy and burn,

Because outside of nuestras tristezas profundas,

Outside of the frescura of our blood derramada

Outside of the estremecimientos of the life and the death

The life goes to be reborn in ti another vez…

translations.title: Here the huellas of the pisadas itself stop...
translations.text:
Here the huellas of the pisadas itself stop;

Here the moon

Lies with the lobos, the perros and the stones,

Behind of the rocks and the carpas, behind of the trees.

Here the moon

Sells your face each night,

For a daga, a vela, a entrelazado of rain.

No arrojes a stone in your fire;

No robes the anillos of vidrio

Of the fingers of the gitanas.

Ellas dormían, thus as the peces and the stones and the trees.


Here the huellas of the pisadas itself stop;

Here the moon estaba pariendo.

¡Gitanas!

Devuéleveles your anillos of vidrio

And the pulseras azules.

translations.title: To G. H. in our cita
translations.text:
Strange amigo mío…

If pudiera llegarte as

yesterday. If asesinas serpientes

no hubieran alborotado all the roads, cavando tumbas for my

gentes and my people, sembrando death and fire.

If no hubiera regado the defeat the land of my homeland

with stones vergonzosas, injuriantes. If this heart that you conoces

outside the mismo that yesterday,

and no sangrase for the puñalada.

If today, amigo mío, as yesterday, pudiera envanecerme of my people, of

my house and my strength,

already mismo me tendrías to your lado.

Amarrando to the playas of your love the barco of my life.

And seríamos igual that two pichones.

translations.title: The end...
translations.text:
The end

of my long road

until where I llegue, in cualquier destino,

is the premio of the años

no the of llegar.

¿For what me apresuro? ¿What I want

of my viaje

for esos desiertos

as a shadow fugitiva?

My pies consumidos for the rocks

the olas of the wind that siguen giving vueltas

and vueltas conmigo

while I sigo to través of this vacío

of this soledad.

Dust, dust

delante and behind mío; to my alrededor, dust.

Corro and corro; and in my hands

only the ilusión, nothing.

Cansada, cansada.

The end

of my long road,

although this itself alargue,

of cualquier destino,

is the premio of the años,

no the of llegar.

translations.title: The day in that we knew the death and the betrayal...
translations.text:
The day in that we knew the death and the betrayal,

itself hizo atrás the marea,

the ventanas of the sky itself cerraron,

and the city contuvo your alientos.

The day of the repliegue of the olas; the day

in that the pasión abominable itself destapara the face,

itself redujo to cenizas the hope,

and my sad city itself asfixió

to the tragarse the sorrow.


Without ecos and without rastros,

the children, the songs, itself perdieron.

Desnuda, with the pies ensangrentados,

the sadness itself drags in my city;

the silence domina my city,

a silence plantado as monte,

dark as night;

a terrible silence, that transporta

the peso of the death and the defeat.


¡Ay, my sad city enmudecida!

¿Pueden thus quemarse the frutos and the mieses,

in time of cosecha?

¡Doloroso end of the recorrido!

translations.title: The flood and the tree
translations.text:
The day in that the diabólico ciclón itself propagó tiránico.

The day in that costas salvajes arrojaron

the dark flood

against the land buena and green,

gritaron (and to través of the aires, your “albricias”

resonaron for all the agencias):

Has fallen the tree.

The poderoso tronco is aplastado.

Already, ni a asomo of life for the tree

dejó the tempestad.


The tree has fallen…

¡Forgive, rojos arroyos!

¡Forgive, raíces regadas

with the vino that sangran the cadáveres!

¡Forgive, raíces árabes,

hundidas as rocks in the entraña,

and that each vez more you entrañáis!


The tree itself will rise.

The tree itself will rise, and your branches,

to the sun, irán creciendo;

in risas verdeciendo, and in leaves,

face to the sun.

And the bird will come,

no has more remedio that venir.

The bird will come.

The bird will come.

translations.title: Behind of your walls
translations.text:
A injusta hand lo has built

and permanece of your tamaño

as a eterna misery.

I have visto your melancólicos muros,

desgastados and deteriorados for the largas centurias, gritando:

¡You me quitas the light and the freedom,

but no you will be able extinguir in my heart

the chispa of the hope!


Cursed, existirás for sofocar each dream

that itself regenera in the medida that itself alimenta.

My heart never dejará of soñar

incluso if this cell itself cerrara for siempre.


If thousand chains me atan

tantas fantásticas wings me harán fly.

Maldeciré to each persona and the of your futuro for the time that pueda.

Because no me doblegará, never seré silenciado

delante of the furia.


Never dejaré of be free.

Voy to sing the deseos of my espíritu,

incluso if vas to aplastarme with chains.

My song manará to raudales from the fondo.

translations.title: To Cristo
translations.text:
Sir, glory of the universes

This año in your cumpleaños

All the alegría of Jerusalén has sido crucified

¡All the bells, Oh Sir

Are in silence!

For two thousand años,

No have estado in silence in your cumpleaños,

To excepción of this año

The cúpulas now are of luto

Lo black is envuelto in black

In the Vía Dolorosa,

Jerusalén is azotado

Bajo the cross

Is bleeding

In the hands of the verdugo.

The world is inflexible ante the tragedia

The light itself has apartado of that despiadado maestro lost

That no encendió a vela

That no derramó a sola lágrima

For lavar the penas of Jerusalén

The labradores have matado to the heredero, Oh Sir,

And usurpado the vid

The labradores mataron to the heredero, my Sir

The bird of the sin itself has dispersado

Inside of the sinners of the world

And voló to profanar the castidad of Jerusalén

What cursed diablo is,

Odiado incluso for the Diablo.

Oh, Sir, glory of Jerusalén

Outside of the pozo of agonía

Outside of the abismo

Outside of the recovecos of the night

Outside of the horror

The moan of Jerusalén asciende to ti

Misericordia, Sir

¡Libérale this chalice!

translations.title: No I will sell this love
translations.text:
What azar

Sweet parecido to a dream azar

Us reunió here in this land distant

Here two souls extrañas nosotros

Were unidos for the Musa

That us llevó of viaje

Nuestras souls convirtiéndose in a song

Flotando in a air of Mozart

In your precioso world

You dijiste: What profundos your eyes

What sweet are

Lo dijiste with a silent, resonante desire

Already that no estábamos solos

And in your eyes a invitación

And in my profundidades intoxicación

What intoxicación

Am a woman thus that discúlpale to my heart your vanidad

When your murmullo lo acaricia: What profundos your eyes

What sweet are


Oh Poet, in my country

My amado country

Tengo a enamorado esperando

Él is my compatriota no I have of derrochar

Your heart

Él is my compatriota no I will sell

Your love

For the tesoros of the world

For the brillantes stars

For the Moon

Without embargo the intoxicación aferra my heart

While in your eyes derivan sombras of love

And the invitación centellea

As a light trémula


Am a woman of modo that perdónale to my heart your vanidad

When your murmullo lo acaricia: What profundos your eyes

What sweet are.

translations.title: Each song
translations.text:
Each song

is a remanso

of the love.


Each lucero,

a remanso

of the time.

A nudo

of the time.


And each suspiro

a remanso

of the cry.

translations.title: To the ear of a muchacha
translations.text:
No quise.

No quise decirte nothing.


Vi in your eyes

two arbolitos locos.

Of brisa, of laughter and of oro.

Itself meneaban.

No quise.

No quise decirte nothing.

translations.title: The six cuerdas
translations.text:
The guitar

makes to cry to the dreams.

The sollozo of the souls

perdidas

itself escapa for your mouth

redonda.

And as the tarántula,

weaves a gran star

for cazar suspiros,

that flotan in your black

cistern of madera.

translations.title: Trees
translations.text:
¡Trees!
¿Have you sido flechas
caídas of the azul?
¿What terribles guerreros you lanzaron?
¿Have sido the stars?


Your music vienen of the soul of the birds,
of the eyes of Dios,
of the pasión perfecta.
¡Arboles!
¿Conocerán your raíces toscas
my heart in land?

translations.title: Is truth
translations.text:
¡Ay, what work me cuesta

to love you as you I want!

For your love me hurts the air,

the heart

and the sombrero.

¿Quién me would buy to mí

this cintillo that tengo

and this sadness of hilo

white, for make pañuelos?

¡Ay, what work me cuesta

to love you as you I want!




Libro of poemas
, 1921

translations.title: "In memoriam"
translations.text:
Sweet chopo,
sweet chopo,
you has puesto
of oro.
Yesterday estabas green,
a green mad
of birds
gloriosos.
Today estás abatido
bajo the sky of August
as I bajo the sky
of my espíritu red.
The fragancia cautiva
of your tronco
will come to my heart
piadoso.
¡Rudo abuelo of the prado!
Nosotros
us hemos puesto
of oro.

translations.title: Questions
translations.text:
A full of cicadas has the field.
¿What you say, Marco Aurelio,
of these old philosophers of the llano?
¡Poor is your pensamiento!


Runs the water of the river mansamente.
¡Oh Sócrates! ¿What ves
in the water that goes to the bitter death?
¡Poor and sad is your fe!


Itself deshojan the roses in the lodo.
¡Oh sweet Juan of Dios!
¿What ves in these pétalos gloriosos?
¡Chico is your heart!

translations.title: Desire
translations.text:
Only your heart hot,
and nothing more.


My paraíso a field
without ruiseñor
ni liras,
with a river discreto
and a fuentecilla.


Without the espuela of the wind
over the fronda,
ni the star that quiere
be leaf.


A enorme light
that outside
luciérnaga
of another,
in a field
of gazes rotas.


A reposo claro
and there our besos,
lunares sonoros
of the echo,
itself abrirían very far.


And your heart hot,
nothing more.

translations.title: Field
translations.text:
The sky is of ceniza.
The trees are blancos,
and are negros carbones
the rastrojos quemados.
Has blood reseca
the wound of the Ocaso,
and the papel incoloro
of the monte is arrugado.
The dust of the road
itself hides in the barrancos,
are the fountains turbias
and quietos the remansos.
Sounds in a gris rojizo
the esquila of the rebaño,
and the noria materna
acabó your rosary.


The sky is of ceniza,
the trees are blancos.

translations.title: A bell
translations.text:
A bell serene
crucified in your ritmo
define to the morning
with peluca of mist
and arroyos of tears.
My old chopo
turbio of ruiseñores
esperaba
put between the hierbas
your branches
mucho antes that the autumn
lo dorara.
But the puntales
of my gazes
lo sostenían.
¡Old chopo, aguarda!
¿No you feel the madera
of my love torn?
Tiéndete in the pradera
when cruja my soul,
that a vendaval of besos
and words
has left rendida,
lacerada.

translations.title: Courtyard húmedo
translations.text:
The spiders
iban for the laurels.
The casualidad
itself goes tornando in snow,
and the años dormidos
already itself atreven
to clavar the telares
of the siempre.


The quietud hecha esfinge
itself laughs of the Death
that sings melancólica
in a grupo
of lejanos cypresses.


The yedra of the gotas
tapiza the walls
empapadas of arcaicos
misereres.


¡Oh tower old! Cries
your tears mudéjares
over this grave courtyard
that no has fountain.


The spiders
iban for the laurels.

translations.title: The balada of the water of the sea
translations.text:
The sea
sonríe to lo far.
Teeth of foam,
lips of sky.


¿What vendes, oh young turbia
with the senos to the air?


Vendo, sir, the water
of the mares.


¿What you carry, oh black young,
mezclado with your blood?


I carry, sir, the water
of the mares.


Those tears salobres
¿of dónde vienen, mother?


Lloro, sir, the water
of the mares.


Heart, and this bitterness
seria, ¿of dónde nace?


¡Bitter mucho the water
of the mares!


The sea
sonríe to lo far.
Teeth of foam,
lips of sky.

translations.title: The poet says the truth
translations.text:
I want to cry my sorrow and you lo I say

for that you me you want and me llores

in a anochecer of ruiseñores

with a puñal, with besos and contigo.


I want kill to the único witness

for the asesinato of my flowers

and convertir my weeping and my sudores

in eterno montón of hard wheat.


That no itself acabe never the skein

of the you I want me you want, siempre ardida

with decrépito sun and moon old.


That lo that no me des and no you pida

será for the death, that no leaves

ni shadow for the carne estremecida.

translations.title: Soneto of the sweet queja
translations.text:
Tengo fear to lose the wonder

of your eyes of statue and the accent

that me puts of night in the mejilla

the solitaria rose of your breath.


Tengo sorrow of be in this shore

tronco without branches, and lo that more I feel

is no tener the flower, pulpa or arcilla,

for the gusano of my suffering.


If you are the treasure hidden mío,

if are my cross and my pain mojado,

if am the dog of your dominion.


No me dejes lose lo that I have won

and decorates the aguas of your river

with leaves of my Autumn enajenado.

translations.title: Love of my entrañas, viva death...
translations.text:
Love of my entrañas, viva death,

in vano espero your word written

and pienso, with the flower that itself marchita,

that if vivo without mí I want perderte.


The air is inmortal. The stone inert

ni conoce the shadow ni the evita.

Heart interior no necesita

the miel helada that the moon vierte.


But I you sufrí. Rasgué my venas,

tiger and dove, over your cintura

in duelo of bites and lilies.


Full then of words my madness

or déjame vivir in my serene

night of the soul for siempre dark.

translations.title: The love duerme in the pecho of the poet
translations.text:
You never entenderás lo that you I want

because duermes in mí and estás asleep.

I you hidden crying, perseguido

for a voice of penetrante acero.


Norma that shakes igual carne and lucero

traspasa already my pecho dolorido

and the turbias words have mordido

the wings of your espíritu severo.


Grupo of people salta in the gardens

esperando your body and my agonía

in horses of light and verdes manes.


But sigue durmiendo, life mía.

Hear my blood rota in the violins.

¡Look that us acechan todavía!

translations.title: The poet speaks for teléfono with the love
translations.text:
Your voice regó the dune of my pecho

in the sweet cabina of madera.

For the sur of my pies was spring

and to the norte of my forehead flower of helecho.


Pine of light for the space estrecho

cantó without alborada and sementera

and my weeping prendió for vez first

crowns of hope for the ceiling.


Sweet and distant voice for mí vertida.

Sweet and distant voice for mí gustada.

Distant and sweet voice amortecida.


Distant as dark doe wound.

Sweet as a sollozo in the snowfall.

¡Distant and sweet in tuétano metida!

translations.title: The concert interrumpido
translations.text:
Has roto the harmony
of the night deep
the calderón helado and soñoliento
of the half moon.


The irrigation channels protestan sordamente
arropadas with juncias,
and the frogs, muecines of the shadow,
itself have quedado mudas.


In the old tavern of the poblado
cesó the sad music,
and has puesto the sordina to your aristón
the star more antigua.


The wind itself has sentado in the torcales
of the mountain dark,
and a chopo solitario, the Pitágoras
of the casta llanura,
quiere dar with your hand centenaria
a cachete to the moon.

translations.title: This light, this fire that devora...
translations.text:
This light, this fire that devora.

This paisaje gris that me rodea.

This pain for a sola idea.

This angustia of sky, world and hora.


This weeping of blood that decorates

lira without pulso already, lúbrica tea.

This peso of the sea that me golpea.

This alacrán that for my pecho mora.


Are guirnaldas of love, cama of wounded,

where without dream, dream your presencia

between the ruinas of my pecho hundido.


And although busco the cumbre of prudencia

me da your heart valle tendido

with cicuta and pasión of bitter ciencia.

translations.title: Night above the two with moon full...
translations.text:
Night above the two with moon full,

I me puse to to cry and you reías.

Your desdén was a dios, the quejas mías

momentos and doves in chain.


Night below the two. Cristal of sorrow,

llorabas you for hondas lejanías.

My pain was a grupo of agonías

over your débil heart of sand.


The dawn us unió over the cama,

the bocas puestas over the chorro helado

of a blood without fin that itself derrama.


And the sun entró for the balcón closed

and the coral of the life abrió your branch

over my heart amortajado.

translations.title: This squab of the Turia that you mando...
translations.text:
This squab of the Turia that you mando,

of dulces eyes and of blanca feather,

over laurel of Grecia vierte and suma

llama lenta of love do estoy parando.


Your cándida virtud, your neck blando,

in limo doble of hot foam,

with a temblor of escarcha, perla and bruma

the ausencia of your mouth is marcando.


Passes the hand over your whiteness

and verás what snowfall melody

esparce in copos over your beauty.


Thus my heart of night and day,

preso in the prison of the love dark,

cries, without verte, your melancholy.

translations.title: The moon and the death
translations.text:
The moon has teeth of ivory.
¡What old and sad appears!
Are the cauces secos,
the campos without verdores
and the trees withered
without nests and without leaves.
Doña Death, arrugada,
walks for sauzales
with your absurdo cortejo
of ilusiones remotas.
Goes vendiendo colores
of cera and of storm
as a hada of cuento
bad and enredadora.


The moon le has comprado
pinturas to the Death.
In this night turbia
¡is the moon mad!


I while so much pongo
in my pecho sombrío
a fair without music
with the tents of shadow.
